pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/client.ts:1 This context is a client-side query cache over Tauri IPC (readCommand -> backend().invoke). It has no store, no query language, no rows and no transactions, so the repository/data-access doctrine does not govern it (client-fetch-cache does); a case-insensitive search of lib/data for rusqlite, sqlite, insert into, execute_batch and query_row found nothing.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/invoke.ts:9 Every read goes through one IPC Backend; no store handle exists on the client side.

pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:13 counterparties.deals_closed is a stored derived count with no writer, no recomputation and no parity check. It reads 0 forever, while the real count is computed live by a subquery (crates/table-ledger/src/display.rs:21), so the schema carries a cached lie that any direct reader of the column would trust.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:13 Stored count with no named recomputation, propagation contract or parity check. git grep finds no writer; the projection recomputes it instead. Already in the scan-sweep backlog (w7-ledger-repos-schema #6).
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0012_deal_groups.sql:3 The at-most-one-agreement invariant names its unit of work, and the deals_group_agrees_once trigger enforces it underneath.
crates/table-ledger/src/tests.rs:168 The test store is built by the production migration chain (Ledger::in_memory), and a test checks that every file is included once, in order.
crates/table-ledger/src/lib.rs:61 The migrations are include_str'd only by the ledger crate, which keeps the connection pub(crate).
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:47 There is one engine (SQLite via rusqlite) and no second driver; invariants are declared in SQLite triggers.
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:15 The schema is static DDL shipped in code; operators define no record types at runtime.
crates/table-ledger/migrations/0001_table.sql:43 The audit stream lives in one transactional store, and the engine sequence orders it; no stream spans stores with different durability.

pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/counter/model.ts:1 These are UI modules and pure display models that read through the client query hooks (useQuery over IPC). A case-insensitive search of their directories (modules/counter, modules/tables, lib/words, mock, console/areas, console/layers) for rusqlite, sqlite, insert into, execute_batch and query_row found nothing. Per-deal reads such as counterparty_note load on demand, not per list row.
